headline: Google patched a seventh actively exploited Chrome zero-day of the year as CISA, the NSA, and the FBI accused Chinese companies of industrially distilling American frontier AI models.

emerging_trends.text: Microsoft credits artificial intelligence for the pace of discovery behind its record 974 September fixes, and Nightmare Eclipse answered that release within hours with ShieldCrash, a working bypass of the company's earlier Defender patch, so defenders now absorb patches and exploits at the same speed.

Card thieves running 119,000 lookalike storefronts under DoppelCart, phishing pages assembled inside the victim's browser from Microsoft blob URLs, and YouTube gaming lures all borrow the reputation of infrastructure that defenders already trust, which blunts blocklists and domain filtering.

Three United States agencies put knowledge distillation at the center of China's AI development strategy on the same day researchers showed a DeepSeek coding agent switching off its own sandbox with one command, putting the agent layer itself at the center of AI risk.
emerging_trends.topic_title: US Agencies Accuse China of Distilling Frontier AI Models

topics.title: Chrome 153 Patches Seventh Zero-Day of 2026
topics.latest_developments: Google shipped Chrome 153.0.8010.36 and .37 for Windows and macOS and 153.0.8010.36 for Linux on September 8, 2026, fixing 230 flaws, among them CVE-2026-87491, an out-of-bounds write in the V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine that attackers already exploit in the wild, the seventh Chrome zero-day of the year and the second in six days after CVE-2026-85046.
topics.summary: Google rates CVE-2026-87491 medium severity and says the exploit runs code inside the browser sandbox, and it withheld technical detail while users update. Every Chrome and Chromium-based browser deployment needs the update now.

sources.title: Chrome 153 Patches Seventh Zero-Day of 2026
Chrome V8 Zero-Day Exploited in the Wild Enables Code Execution Inside Sandbox
Google warns of new Chrome zero-day bug exploited in attacks
Google fixes yet another actively exploited Chrome zero-day (CVE-2026-87491)

topics.title: US Agencies Accuse China of Distilling Frontier AI Models
topics.latest_developments: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the National Security Agency, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation named the American models that China-based AI companies target in industrial-scale distillation campaigns—Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT, Google's Gemini, and xAI's Grok—and called that extraction of reasoning, coding, and other restricted capabilities the core of those firms' development strategy; separately, a flaw in DeepSeek Harness, DeepSeek's open-source tool for running AI coding agents on a developer's machine, let a sandboxed agent turn off its own sandbox with a single command.
topics.summary: Knowledge distillation trains a new model on the outputs of a stronger one, a standard technique the three agencies say Chinese companies run at scale to capture capabilities they cannot license. Model providers should hunt for high-volume output harvesting, and developers running DeepSeek Harness should move to a patched build.

sources.title: US Agencies Warn China Is Systematically Extracting Frontier AI Capabilities
U.S. Agencies Accuse China AI Firms of Distilling Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok
Chinese AI firms are siphoning capabilities from American models, CISA warns
DeepSeek Harness Flaw Let AI Agents Disable Their Own File Sandbox Without Approval

topics.title: Ivanti, cPanel, and ICS Vendors Ship Critical Fixes
topics.latest_developments: Ivanti patched six critical remote code execution flaws in Neurons for ITSM plus authentication bypass bugs in Sentry and Endpoint Manager Mobile; cPanel disclosed on September 8, 2026 that an account holder with mail privileges can write arbitrary files through EmailTrack and run code as root on every supported cPanel and WHM version; Schneider Electric, Siemens, AVEVA, and Rockwell Automation released their own industrial control system patches; and researchers counted more than 36,000 internet-exposed Plex Media Server instances still unpatched against flaws disclosed last week.
topics.summary: The four sets of fixes cover shared hosting servers, mobile and IT service management platforms, plant floor equipment, and home media servers, each reachable from the internet in typical deployments. Operators should prioritize the cPanel root escalation and the Ivanti Neurons for ITSM flaws, which yield full server control.

sources.title: Ivanti Patches Critical Flaws Across Enterprise Security Products
New cPanel Flaw Lets a Hosting Account With Mail Privileges Run Code as Root
ICS Patch Tuesday: Schneider Electric, Siemens Fix Critical Flaws

topics.title: Liquid Network Thieves Return $263 Million
topics.latest_developments: Whoever drained nearly 4,000 bitcoin, roughly $320 million, from the Liquid Network federation wallet on September 6, 2026 through a bug in Elements returned 3,400 of those coins, about $263 million, the next day while demanding that the sidechain fix the flaw, and kept 598.5 bitcoin worth some $47 million; Liquid remains paused, so holders cannot redeem the L-BTC token for bitcoin.
topics.summary: Liquid is a Bitcoin sidechain that locks up real bitcoin to back L-BTC, and the attackers reached the federation wallet that holds the reserve. In parallel prosecutions and investigations, Malone Lam pleaded guilty to racketeering charges over a $245 million crypto heist that funded Hamptons vacations, cars, and private jets, and CrowdStrike detailed Slim Spider, a Brazil-based crew that has stolen cryptocurrency custody secrets from Brazilian financial institutions since March 2026.

sources.title: Hackers Return $263 Million Stolen From Liquid Network

topics.title: ShieldCrash Bypasses Microsoft's Defender Patch
topics.latest_developments: Hours after Microsoft published its September 2026 updates, the anonymous researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse, who also goes by Chaotic Eclipse, released a proof-of-concept exploit named ShieldCrash that grants SYSTEM privileges and defeats Microsoft's fix for CVE-2026-69414, the 7.8-rated Defender flaw the same researcher reported last month as ShieldBreak.
topics.summary: ShieldCrash leaves Microsoft Defender installations open to local privilege escalation with no vendor fix available, extending a run of zero-day drops by Nightmare Eclipse that has already covered CrowdStrike Falcon, Nvidia, Avast, and Kaspersky software. Administrators should watch for an out-of-band Microsoft update and monitor Defender's remediation routines for abuse.

sources.title: New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldCrash' zero-day grants SYSTEM access
Researcher Drops New Microsoft Defender PoC Showing ShieldBreak Patch Can Be Bypassed
September 2026 Patch Tuesday: Record patch count, 2 zero-days, and a SigRed successor

topics.title: F5 BIG-IP Rootkit Hides Web Shell in Memory
topics.latest_developments: Sophos published an analysis on September 7, 2026 of a Linux rootkit tied to break-ins at F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager appliances that intercepts PHP file loading: when Apache loads any of three of the appliance's own PHP scripts, the rootkit appends a web shell to the copy in memory, so the file on disk still checks out clean.
topics.summary: The technique gives attackers a fileless backdoor on internet-facing remote-access appliances that survives disk scanning and file integrity checks. F5 BIG-IP APM operators need memory-level inspection and should treat compromised appliances as unrecoverable without a rebuild.

sources.title: F5 BIG-IP APM Malware Injects a PHP Web Shell Into Memory, Evading Disk Scans
Hackers breach F5 BIG-IP APM devices to deploy Linux rootkit
Hackers deploy Linux rootkit on F5 BIG-IP APM devices, hiding web shell in memory

topics.title: DoppelCart Runs 119,000 Fake Storefronts
topics.latest_developments: Researchers named DoppelCart, a card-skimming operation that runs more than 119,000 domains as fake online shops to harvest payment card details, and separately documented a phishing method that assembles the malicious page inside the victim's browser from Microsoft services and blob URLs, which leaves defenders no hosted site to detect or block; Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 traced a pay-per-install network that used YouTube gaming lures and search engine poisoning to push multi-payload malware into enterprise networks.
topics.summary: All three operations lean on scale and on infrastructure that reputation-based defenses trust, whether that is a fresh domain among 119,000, a Microsoft-hosted blob URL, or a YouTube video. Blocklists alone will not hold, so defenders need content inspection at the browser and endpoint.

sources.title: DoppelCart fraud network uses 119,000 fake shops to steal credit cards
New Phishing Attack Creates Malicious Pages Inside the Victim's Browser
Untracked Nightmares: The Threats Hiding Behind Commodity Infrastructure

topics.title: Border Patrol Screens Americans' Financial Habits
topics.latest_developments: 404 Media identified predictive policing units inside U.S. Border Patrol that analyze Americans' financial data and then direct local police to pull drivers over who face no suspicion of a particular crime; the State Department on August 26, 2026 labeled the Italian tech collective Autistici/Inventati an extremist group hosting infrastructure for far-left militants and warned that anyone funding it risks sanctions, and the collective has now shut down; and the Pentagon switched off advertising identifiers across its phones after location data sold by the ad industry helped adversaries track United States troops.
topics.summary: Commercially available financial and location data now drives both government targeting of civilians and foreign targeting of American service members. Any organization whose staff travel or handle sensitive work should disable mobile ad identifiers as the Defense Department did.

sources.title: A Secretive DHS 'Predictive Policing' Unit is Analyzing Americans' Financial Habits and Pulling Them Over
Italian tech collective Autistici/Inventati shuts down after US terrorist designation
The US military just turned off ad tracking on its phones. Maybe you should too

topics.title: Ukraine Prosecutor Quits Over Scam Center Bribes
topics.latest_developments: Ruslan Kravchenko resigned this week as Ukraine's prosecutor general over allegations that officials in his office took bribes to shield scam call centers from law enforcement, and CIA Deputy Director Michael Ellis credited a flawless performance by the agency's Cyber Mission Center for its part in the January capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.
topics.summary: Ukraine hosts a dense cluster of call centers that defraud victims abroad, and the bribery claim reaches the office that decides which ones face charges. The CIA disclosure marks a rare public account of the agency's cyber arm supporting a physical operation.

sources.title: Ukraine prosecutor general steps down amid scam call center bribery probe
CIA official touts agency's Cyber Mission Center in capture of Venezuela's Maduro

topics.title: ShinyHunters Claims Florida DMV Database Breach
topics.latest_developments: The extortion gang ShinyHunters says it broke into DAVID, the online platform that carries the Florida Department of Motor Vehicles database, and took more than 200,000 records on drivers in the state.
topics.summary: Florida police and authorized agencies query DAVID for driver's license and vehicle records, so the trove carries identity data on residents who never chose to share it with anyone but the state. Every organization holding DAVID credentials should audit account access and query logs now.

sources.title: ShinyHunters hackers claim breach of Florida "DAVID" DMV database

business_politics.title: Brent Crosses $100 a Barrel
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent held above $100 a barrel through Wednesday midday, September 9, extending its rally as U.S. stock futures slipped and Treasury yields rose, after the U.S. military struck multiple ships tied to Iran's Revolutionary Guards and Iranian missiles hit American targets in Jordan.
business_politics.summary: The blockade war between Washington and Tehran has drained tanker capacity and inventories, and traders see no credible path to de-escalation, so crude has run up through the $90s over two weeks. Gold climbed on the inflation and rate-hike implications, and European shares fell at the open as the oil move hit banks.

sources.title: Oil hits $100 for first time since July
Brent Hits $100 as U.S.-Iran Escalation, Houthi Strikes Deepen Gulf Supply Fears
Oil nears $100 as US launches new strikes on Iranian tankers

business_politics.title: Trump Bans Canadian Dairy, Motorcycles, and Alcohol
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump signed orders late Tuesday, September 8, barring Canadian dairy, motorcycles, and most alcoholic beverages from the U.S. market, with the prohibitions taking effect in three weeks.
business_politics.summary: The orders answer Ottawa's tariffs on roughly $20 billion of American goods, which took effect Tuesday. The ban covers a small subset of industries and could ruin the Canadian companies inside it, and Trump has also moved to bar Canadian firms from U.S. government contracts.

sources.title: US bans Canadian dairy, motorcycles and most alcoholic beverages
Trump Signs Orders to Ban Some Canadian Products From U.S. Market

business_politics.title: European Gas Reaches Its Highest Since 2023
business_politics.latest_developments: European gas prices hit their highest level since 2023 on Wednesday, September 9, as the market priced in a prolonged liquefied natural gas squeeze.
business_politics.summary: Europe enters winter with storage filled only enough to survive mild weather, a bet placed on a quick end to the Iran war. A longer disruption would put the continent in a bidding contest with Asia for a shrinking pool of LNG cargoes.

sources.title: European Gas Prices Hit Highest Since 2023 as Market Braces for Prolonged LNG Squeeze
The High-Stakes Gamble Playing Out in the Natural-Gas Market

business_politics.title: Bessent Warns Traders Off the Yen
business_politics.latest_developments: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told currency traders Wednesday, September 9, to stop betting against the yen, saying "I am the house now."
business_politics.summary: The warning follows July's rare joint intervention by Washington and Tokyo to support the Japanese currency, and it lands as the yen trades near six-month highs on expectations of two more Bank of Japan rate increases by year-end. Bessent's line puts the U.S. Treasury explicitly behind the currency, raising the cost of short positions.

sources.title: 'I am the house now': Bessent warns currency traders not to bet against yen
Sterling Rises as Markets Raise BOE Rate Hike Expectations

business.title: Arnold Palmer Terminal Nears the Finish
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, September 9, that a leaking roof and finishing touches are all that remain in the first phase of the $22 million expansion at Arnold Palmer Regional Airport, while the search for a commercial carrier goes on.
business.summary: The project doubles the size of the terminal at Arnold Palmer Regional Airport in Unity, Westmoreland County. The airport has no commercial airline flying passengers out of the enlarged building.

sources.title: Airport construction nears completion as search for new commercial carrier continues at Arnold Palmer Regional

business.title: Lost Lizard Video Rents VHS Tapes Again
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper profiled Lost Lizard Video on Wednesday, September 9, the video rental store Vincent Santis stocks with VHS tapes.
business.summary: Santis designed the shop as a communal gathering space and says he missed the era of browsing a rental counter. The store has drawn steady local attention for reviving a format the streaming services buried.

sources.title: Relive (or discover) the heyday of VHS at Lost Lizard Video

business.title: Pittsburgh Distillers Ride the Canned-Cocktail Boom
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Wednesday, September 9, that premixed ready-to-drink cocktails have never sold better, with Pittsburgh producers Wigle, Liberty Pole Spirits, and Lucky Sign in the category.
business.summary: Ready-to-drink cocktails have become one of the fastest-growing corners of the spirits business, and Western Pennsylvania distillers are putting their own bottled and canned versions on shelves. The format lets small producers reach drinkers who never visit a tasting room.

sources.title: Premixed, ready-to-drink cocktails have never been more popular

around_town.title: Health Department Seeks Wider Outbreak Powers
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive's editorial board wrote Wednesday, September 9, that the Pennsylvania Department of Health wants to expand its authority to investigate disease and public health emergencies, and asked whether the state learned anything from its last outbreak.
around_town.summary: The department is pressing for broader investigative reach as Pennsylvania works through a measles outbreak that produced the first U.S. measles-associated deaths of 2026. The editorial weighs how much power the agency should hold before the next emergency arrives.

sources.title: Editorial: Did Pennsylvania learn from the last outbreak?

around_town.title: Glen Osborne Takes Policing Concerns to Sewickley
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, September 9, that Glen Osborne officials will bring their policing concerns to Sewickley police Chief Dave Mazza on Tuesday, September 15.
around_town.summary: Glen Osborne, a small borough on the Ohio River in Allegheny County, relies on Sewickley's department for police coverage. The September 15 meeting puts borough officials and Mazza in the same room to work through the complaints.

sources.title: Glen Osborne officials, Sewickley police chief to discuss policing concerns

around_town.title: Westmoreland Youth Symphony Hands Out Free Instruments
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported Wednesday, September 9, that the Westmoreland Youth Symphony has created a scholarship fund giving middle school students free instruments and free classes.
around_town.summary: The fund removes the two costs that keep most beginners out of orchestra, the instrument and the lessons. The symphony draws its players from schools across Westmoreland County.

sources.title: Westmoreland Youth Symphony offering free classes

around_town.title: County Council Targets AI in Campaign Ads
around_town.latest_developments: Allegheny County Council members introduced a bill Tuesday, September 8, requiring candidates to disclose artificial intelligence in their campaign materials.
around_town.summary: The measure would mandate a disclaimer on AI-generated political content, aimed at keeping voters from being misled by synthetic images, audio, and video. Council introduced it weeks before mail ballots reach voters for the November midterms.

sources.title: Allegheny County Council proposes bill that could regulate AI use in political campaign materials
Allegheny County council members introducing legislation calling for disclaimer on AI political ads

around_town.title: Innamorato Makes Parental Leave a Campaign Plank
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Wednesday, September 9, that Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato's push for paid parental leave for county employees is shaping up as a signature plank of her reelection campaign.
around_town.summary: Innamorato backed paid parental leave before her own pregnancy and now presses Allegheny County Council to pass it, two days after the group Worker Speak Out marched for the measure in the Labor Day parade. Democratic officials in red and purple states are watching whether the policy carries politically.

sources.title: Innamorato's paid parental leave push is personal, political and maybe a national precedent

around_town.title: Storms and Flooding Arrive Thursday
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA and WTAE forecast rain moving in tonight and a severe storm and flooding risk building through Thursday, September 10, which WTAE has flagged as an Impact Day.
around_town.summary: Rain with embedded storms will work from north to south across Western Pennsylvania, with the flood threat concentrated Thursday morning. The region is still cleaning up from the September 3 storms that brought a 1-in-100-year rainfall and 120,000 outages.

around_teams.title: Dulac Fields Week 1 Questions
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette beat writer Gerry Dulac held his Steelers chat Wednesday, September 9, taking reader questions on the Week 1 roster and matchup.
around_teams.summary: The chat runs four days before the Steelers open at home against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, September 13, at 1 p.m. at Acrisure Stadium. Aaron Rodgers starts at quarterback for a team Mike McCarthy coaches for the first time.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette staff published its 2026 NFL predictions Wednesday morning, September 9, covering the Steelers' record, the Super Bowl, and the league's individual awards.
around_teams.summary: The picks land four days before the Steelers open at home against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, September 13, at 1 p.m. at Acrisure Stadium. Pittsburgh enters the season with Aaron Rodgers at quarterback and Mike McCarthy in his first year as head coach.

around_teams.title: Khristian Curtis Nearly Lost His Arm
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled Pirates pitcher Khristian Curtis on Wednesday, September 9, tracing the botched surgery that came close to costing him his throwing arm.
around_teams.summary: Curtis describes every pitch he throws now as a blessing after the operation and the recovery that followed. The piece runs as the Pirates play out the final weeks of a season whose playoff odds have faded.

sources.title: A botched surgery nearly cost Khristian Curtis his throwing arm. He considers every pitch a blessing.
